stories.title: Judge postpones US trial for Libyan man charged in 1988 Lockerbie bombing
stories.summary: A federal judge on Monday postponed a trial in the US for a former Libyan intelligence official charged in the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103, citing the discovery of new evidence that defence lawyers want to examine in the nearly 40-year-old case. Jury selection was scheduled to begin on Wednesday for the federal trial of Abu Agila Mohammad Masud Kheir al-Marimi in Washington. His trial will be the first in the US for the December 21, 1988, bombing. US District Judge Dabney Friedrich’s order...

stories.title: German foreign minister acknowledges funding shortfall for military aid to Ukraine
stories.summary: BERLIN, August 25. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has acknowledged a funding shortfall for military aid to Ukraine. "There is indeed not enough money [to pay for weapons for Ukraine], that is true," Wadephul said on ARD television during a visit to Ukraine. He was responding to a journalist's question about whether Berlin should increase support amid an acute funding shortage despite being one of Kiev's key allies. The German foreign minister said he had discussed the matter in detail with Ukraine's new defense minister. "I now need to pass this information on to Berlin and Brussels. Consultations with European foreign ministers, and especially with our [German] Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, will show what more we can do, what others can do, and which funds, perhaps already earmarked for next year, could be allocated a little earlier. This will once again become a shared task for many," Wadephul said. At the same time, he noted he could not say for certain whether this would happen. Russia has repeatedly said that arms supplies to the Kiev regime only prolong the conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: Hyundai Motor, labor union tentatively reach wage deal
stories.summary: The management and labor union of Hyundai Motor Co. tentatively reached a wage agreement early Tuesday following a series of strikes that caused production disruptions. The two sides reached an understanding at the 17th round of talks, agreeing to raise monthly base pay by 100,000 won (US$72.20), provide a performance bonus of more than 400 percent of monthly salary and pay an additional payment of 12.5 million won, according to the union. The two sides also agreed to extend the retirement age from the current 60 to 65 if related laws and regulations are revised. If the agreement is approved in a union vote scheduled for Aug. 31, this year's wage negotiations at South Korea's largest automaker will be concluded. The 400,000-member union staged a combined 60 hours of strikes this year, resulting in about 120 hours of production disruptions across two shifts. The labor action included a full-day strike Friday, the union's first such walkout in 10 years. The strikes are estimated to have caused cumulative production losses of around 55,200 vehicles, with lost sales exceeding 2.3 trillion won, according to industry sources.
